questions.question: What is matter, and what evidence shows that matter is made of moving particles?
questions.expected_answer: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. Perfume sprayed in one corner spreads across the room, and food colouring slowly spreads through still water, which shows that particles move and mix. Sugar stirred into water takes up less space than expected, which shows there are spaces between particles.

questions.question: Describe how particles are arranged and how they move in a solid, a liquid and a gas.
questions.expected_answer: In a solid, particles are packed closely in a regular pattern and only vibrate on the spot, so a solid has a fixed shape and volume. In a liquid, particles are close together but can slide past each other, so a liquid flows and takes the shape of its container but keeps its volume. In a gas, particles are far apart and move fast and freely in all directions, so a gas spreads out to fill any container and can be squashed.

questions.question: Use the particle model to explain melting and boiling.
questions.expected_answer: When a solid is heated, its particles vibrate faster until they break out of their rows and slide past each other, so the solid melts into a liquid. When a liquid is heated, its particles move faster until they escape and spread far apart as a gas, so the liquid boils. The particles themselves stay the same; only their arrangement and movement change.
